summary: Request to add or remove an entity from party participation, read by esv::party::PartySystem::ProcessMemberParticipationRequests (Toolkit EoCServer.dll+0xAAF310) and written only by esv::party::UnitTestHelper on macOS. No Windows function of bg3.exe creates it except the generic adder (bg3.exe+0x2BC64F0), so the member offsets are not established on Windows. The system's own legacy queue (this+0xB0, 16-byte elements: bool toAdd at +0, entity at +8, log text "LEGACY MemberParticipation request: entity (%s) toAdd (%s)") shows the content but not the component's order. Never seen alive. Registry total 16 (server row).

fields.name: Entity
fields.evidence: Windows: bg3.exe+0x2BBB200 (called from the per-frame update of esv::party::PartySystem bg3.exe+0x2BB7AD0) iterates the component's query with stride 0x10 and reads `uVar4 = *puVar15` (8 bytes at +0) and `bVar23 = *(byte*)(puVar15 + 1)` (+8), then appends them to its legacy queue as {byte at +0, handle at +8}; the handle is later checked as an entity (>>0x36 < 0x41, != null) and inserted into a HashSet with FUN_140721030. macOS default constructor agrees.

fields.name: ToAdd
fields.evidence: Windows: bg3.exe+0x2BBB200 reads the byte at +8 and stores it as the flag of the legacy request (whose log text calls it toAdd); macOS default constructor stores 1 at +8 (default true).

fields.name: _Pad9
fields.evidence: Never read by bg3.exe+0x2BBB200; padding to the registry size 16.

open_questions: Name ToAdd is inferred from the legacy request log text, not from a game field name.
Not seen alive (seen.py has no samples).
second_pass: Settled on Windows: the reader bg3.exe+0x2BBB200 of esv::party::PartySystem takes an 8-byte entity handle at +0 and a byte at +8 from each 16-byte component; the macOS order (entity first) is right, the legacy queue just stores them the other way round.
